name: Spirit-Detecting Mirror Technique
description: Air is the most closely connected to the spirit world of all five elements, so it is easier for Aspects of Air to pierce the veil and see the unseen. Invoking a Spirit Mirror requires an ordinary mirror, polished metal, or any reflective surface (even a pool of still water). For the remainder of the scene the Exalt can see nearby spirits reflected in such surfaces and, if they are reflected, hear what they say. A clever Dragon-Blood might do this without the spirits noticing — using a goblet of water and taking a sip now and then, or polishing a sword blade.

name: Harmonious Wind-Luring Song
description: Many Air-aspected Dragon-Blooded learn the ways of the sky-spirits who create the weather and can call them to direct the wind. To do so, the Exalt must speak to the elementals in their own tongue — the sounds of wind sighing over crags and through treetops and the rumbles of thunder — imitating such sounds with voice and bull-roarer, flute, or a wind-plucked harp. Inviting the winds to blow takes five minutes. This basic Charm evokes nothing more than a stiff breeze, still enough to interfere with archery or send a sailing ship scudding at good speed. During the hour of effect the character can control the magic wind's direction by singing for a turn.

name: Spirit-Grounding Shout
description: Often the most effective way to deal with a spirit is to force it into the physical world and defeat it there. The character utters the Spirit-Grounding Shout and reflexive opposed Essence rolls are made for her and the target spirit; if the Exalt wins, the spirit is forced to materialize (if she loses it may remain dematerialized). A successful shout forces manifestation for no less than the Exalt's permanent Essence in minutes. The Essence for materialization (if the spirit is naturally immaterial) is first drained from the spirit's reserves, and any remainder is drained from the Exalt; if there is not enough Essence between them, the spirit remains immaterial but the Essence is still lost. No effect on spirits with permanent Essences higher than the Dragon-Blood's.

name: Spirit-Chaining Strike
description: Immobilizes spirit beings, often the first step toward eliminating them. The character must strike the spirit with an attack, then his player immediately makes a reflexive Intelligence + Occult roll (difficulty = the spirit's Essence). Each extra success imposes a one-die penalty to all actions the spirit takes; if the penalty exceeds the spirit's Essence, it is immobilized and unable to act for the rest of the scene. Subsequent uses are additive so long as the Charm never lapses, and Spirit Chains from other Dragon-Blooded are additive as well. It affects a spirit whether manifested or not, but the character must be able to perceive and strike it to bind it. Explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.

name: Spirit-Shredding Attack
description: Sometimes a spirit must be destroyed. Invoking this Charm requires a successful physical attack against a spirit (it must be materialized and/or the character must have some way to affect it). The blow does normal damage to spirits; in addition, the attacker's player reflexively rolls Willpower + Essence against a difficulty of the spirit's Essence, and each extra success reduces the spirit's temporary Essence by an amount equal to the Dragon-Blooded's permanent Essence. The character does not absorb the Essence — it dissipates. A spirit destroyed by a Spirit-Shredding Attack is irrevocably gone.

name: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery
description: Handling the mysteries of sorcery is far more difficult for the Terrestrial Exalted than for the Anathema; the enchantments of the Celestial and Solar circles are beyond the Dragon-Blooded, but Terrestrial Circle sorcery is available to them once this Charm is learned. Invoking this Charm only enables the character to cast a single Terrestrial Circle sorcery spell; the spell itself has an Essence cost, often very high, listed in the spell's description, that the character must pay to actualize it. Terrestrial Circle Sorcery can never be part of a Combo.

name: Minding the Dragon's Eggs
description: All Dragon-Blooded can harmonize themselves with the elemental pole with which they share aspect in order to orient themselves. Study, in ages past, of the mechanism of this phenomenon provided the inspiration for a number of techniques by which Terrestrial Exalts could learn to harmonize their Essences in other ways. Most common of these techniques is this Charm, which allows harmony with the Magical Material of the Dragon-Blooded: jade. This Charm is a staple of surveyors, criminals and the Jade Sniffers of the Thousand Scales. A character using this Charm can sense the direction to jade of her elemental aspect up to a range of her Essence x 200 yards without rolling. Successes on a Perception + Occult roll allow the character to glean more detailed information from the Charm, with each success allowing for either the perception of another of the four remaining elemental forms of jade or a rough indication of the amount of an already-detected quantity of jade. This Charm is ineffective against jade that is attuned to someone other than the character using the Charm, due to the interference of the attuned individual's anima. Jade that is on the person of someone using magic to conceal his presence or in a site that has had such magic worked on it will only be detected if the Perception + Occult roll succeeds versus a difficulty equal to the successes rolled to activate the obfuscatory magic or the Essence of the character using the magic (whichever is higher).

name: Fivefold Resonance Sense
description: Using a refined version of the technique behind Minding the Dragon's Eggs, a Terrestrial occultist can now use her Essence sense to detect quantities of the other Magical Materials: starmetal, orichalcum, moonsilver and soulsteel. This Charm works exactly as Minding the Dragon's Eggs, but only to a range of the character's Essence x 50 yards.

name: Seeing the Maker's Hand
description: With much of the documentation lost on how magical artifacts were crafted in the First Age, modern savants must often reverse engineer items as best they are able in order to better understand how to recreate or service them. Additionally, many artifacts of modern make are one-of-a-kind constructions, and it is safest to have the fullest possible knowledge of an unfamiliar item before attempting to work with it. To this end, Terrestrial technicians have learned to apply the sensory techniques of Essence-harmonizing to better analyze the fundamental material construction and Essence-channeling of artifacts. To enact this Charm, the character must handle the item in question as if he were attempting to attune to it before spending the required Essence and before his player makes a Perception + Occult roll with a difficulty of the item's Artifact rating. Artifacts specifically designed so that their properties are difficult to identify may have a higher difficulty. Success on this roll immediately gives the character a rough indication of the item's power level, as reflected by the Artifact rating, with additional successes providing more detailed insight about the specific abilities of the item. Very powerful or complex artifacts may require multiple uses of Seeing the Maker's Hand over time to fully understand their workings. This Charm is ineffective on artifacts that are attuned to an owner.

name: Embracing the Arcane
description: Sorcery and magical engineering are inherently dangerous undertakings, as many crippled former Heptagram servants can attest. The slightest misstep when summoning a demon or miscalculation in Manse design can have spectacular and fatal consequences for everyone in the area. Diligence is, of course, the most important habit to develop to avoid these is-sues, but the frequency with which dangerous magic must be worked in the Realm means that it is often only a matter of time before a disaster occurs. High-end professional magical practitioners use this Charm as one of many safeguards against terrible accidents, in addition to the obvious advantages of straightforward mastery of a particular discipline. This Charm allows a character to convert his Occult specialty dice into automatic success for 2 motes of Essence per die converted. This only works if the character is exercising his specialty.
